record.original_question: What is the largest constant C such that, for every sufficiently large graph G of order n with lambda(G) > sqrt(floor(n^2/4)), G contains a cycle of every length ell <= (C - epsilon)n for all positive epsilon < C?

evidence.quote: Problem 3 (Nikiforov [116]). What is the maximum C such that for all positive ε < C and sufficiently large n, every graph G of order n with λ(G) > sqrt(⌊n^2/4⌋) contains a cycle of length ℓ for every integer ℓ ≤ (C − ε)n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix. Determine the largest constant $C>0$ with the following property: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,C)$, there exists $n_0=n_0(\varepsilon)$ such that every graph $G$ of order $n\ge n_0$ satisfying
$$\lambda(G) > \sqrt{\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor}$$
contains a cycle of length $\ell$ for every integer $3\le \ell \le (C-\varepsilon)n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is generally regarded as open. Partial progress has been made: lower bounds on the constant $C$ have been established (e.g., $C\ge 1/160$ by Ning–Peng, and improvements such as $C\ge 1/7$ and $C\ge 1/4$ in subsequent works by Li and collaborators), but the exact value of the largest admissible $C$ is not known.

status_evidence.title: Eigenvalues and cycles of consecutive lengths
status_evidence.snippet: Improved lower bounds on the constant C in Nikiforov's problem on cycles of consecutive lengths under a spectral radius condition.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: improved lower bound on C, but exact maximum C remains open.

status_evidence.title: The stability method, eigenvalues and cycles of consecutive lengths
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes lower bounds toward Nikiforov's problem on consecutive cycle lengths.
status_evidence.claim: Problem still open with only lower bounds known.
